workflow.description: Confirm live position, manifest identity, ignition events, test-drive track coherence and one live alert round-trip per unit
workflow.gate: no vehicle returns to service without a recorded pass or a triage entry

workflow.description: Bucket failures as power, GPS, cellular or human; one fix attempt per bucket then swap; label pulled units for the bench
workflow.gate: every failure carries a bucket and discriminator evidence; no unresolved unit left off the exception list

workflow.action: Configure geofences, alerts and reports to the workflow, then train the admin
workflow.description: Draw consumed fences, tune the backbone alert set with named recipients, schedule decision-mapped reports, then run role-sized training and book the week-one review
workflow.gate: every fence, alert and report names its consumer; each user demonstrates their routine; week-one review scheduled

workflow.description: Aggregate verification passes and exceptions, confirm disclosure and training, deliver the documentation pack, demonstrate the intake questions on live data, obtain signature
workflow.artifact: signed acceptance with exception list and delivered pack
workflow.gate: all conditions met or dated-and-owned on the exception list; subscription clock and operations handoff start at signature

priority_rationale: The frame nodes - intake, the lawful-use gate and the regulatory flag map - come first because every device, install and configuration choice reads from what the fleet is, what may lawfully be tracked, and which obligation classes are in play; device-family and coverage decisions precede physical install design because a family misfit is a re-order while a design fix is an afternoon; platform structure, pairing and disclosure precede install day so the yard work is matching and mounting rather than provisioning and improvising; and verification, triage, documentation and the acceptance gate close the sequence because they convert finished installs into a proven, disclosed, documented fleet that recurring operations can inherit without re-deriving it.

dominance_rules.rule: The lawful-use gate dominates every install, configuration and revenue consideration
dominance_rules.rationale: a single covert-tracking job outweighs any deal size in legal exposure and in what the business becomes
dominance_rules.trigger: any request to track without authorization or disclosure, however framed
dominance_rules.action: refuse per the script, log the refusal, and decline adjacent workarounds such as hidden-from-drivers mounting

dominance_rules.rule: Serviceability dominates concealment absent documented risk
dominance_rules.rationale: hidden mounts are a permanent labor tax on every future touch, so hiding must be bought with a reason
dominance_rules.trigger: a mount decision tends toward deep concealment by default or by customer vibe
dominance_rules.action: hold the shallowest mount meeting the documented tamper/theft risk for that class, and photograph whatever depth is chosen

dominance_rules.rule: The workmanship standard dominates schedule pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: an electrical fault attributed to the installer costs more than any batch delay
dominance_rules.trigger: bay-time overruns tempt the crew to skip fusing, dressing or photos
dominance_rules.action: shrink the batch or add a window; reopen and re-do any unit found below standard before verification

dominance_rules.rationale: an unverified fleet disperses to job sites and converts every latent defect into a truck-chase
dominance_rules.trigger: the customer or the schedule pushes to skip test drives or alert round-trips
dominance_rules.action: no vehicle returns to service unverified; the remainder moves to the fallback window

dominance_rules.rule: The pairing manifest dominates memory, labels' vibes and 'it must be that van'
dominance_rules.rationale: identity errors poison every downstream report and surface as customer-facing disputes weeks later
dominance_rules.trigger: any doubt about which device sits in which vehicle
dominance_rules.action: re-verify identity against the manifest by moving the vehicle; never guess or patch the platform name to fit

dominance_rules.rule: The regulatory verification flag dominates sales claims
dominance_rules.rationale: a compliance promise the certification does not back transfers the customer's regulatory risk onto the reseller
dominance_rules.trigger: a sale or configuration drifts toward presenting tracking as ELD/HOS compliance
dominance_rules.action: state the GPS-is-not-an-ELD boundary, name the obligation class, and require verified certification before any compliance language ships

dominance_rules.rationale: an undisclosed rollout breaches the lawful posture and manufactures the sabotage triage will chase for months
dominance_rules.trigger: install day arrives before acknowledgments are collected
dominance_rules.action: install hardware if scheduled, but units stay dark until the disclosure record completes

dominance_rules.rule: The fleet's actual workflow dominates platform defaults
dominance_rules.rationale: default config answers nobody's question and rots into an unused account, which is where churn begins
dominance_rules.trigger: onboarding tends toward shipping the default report pack and everything-on alerts
dominance_rules.action: configure only artifacts that name an intake question and a consumer; prune the rest

dominance_rules.rule: A named acting recipient dominates alert completeness
dominance_rules.rationale: an alert nobody owns is negative value - it buries the alert someone does own
dominance_rules.trigger: an alert is proposed 'to be safe' without an owner or expected action
dominance_rules.action: do not configure it; record the decision so the week-one review can revisit with evidence

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete the per-unit intake sheet before ordering any hardware
anti_rework_rules.prevents: family-level device misfits that surface as fleet-wide re-orders and re-installs

anti_rework_rules.rule: Qualify coverage in the fleet's actual operating areas before committing a SKU fleet-wide
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a coverage-hole or network-sunset discovery forcing a full hardware swap after deployment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the naming convention and account structure before the first device is paired
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mass renaming and re-grouping after reports have shipped with the wrong names in them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Bench-activate and manifest-label every device before install day
anti_rework_rules.prevents: yard-side provisioning queues, box swaps, and pairing errors discovered in payroll disputes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Collect driver acknowledgments before units go live
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the resentment-driven unplug and grievance wave that a surprise rollout manufactures

anti_rework_rules.rule: Prove the per-model hardwire design on the first unit of each model before running the batch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repeating a ghost-ignition or bad-tap mistake across every identical vehicle in the fleet

anti_rework_rules.rule: Photograph mounts and tap points before panels close
anti_rework_rules.prevents: teardown expeditions on every future service call and warranty dispute

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify each unit before its vehicle returns to service
anti_rework_rules.prevents: chasing dispersed vehicles across job sites to fix what the bay would have caught in seconds

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tune alerts with the admin in the co-piloted first week
anti_rework_rules.prevents: alert-fatigue habits that calcify into an ignored account and a rescue re-onboarding at renewal time

iteration_protocol.action: route to triage while installer and vehicle are co-located, bucket the fault, fix or swap, re-verify

iteration_protocol.trigger: a failure class repeats across units - same model ghost trips, same SKU no-fix, same mount position blind
iteration_protocol.action: stop the batch, update the device matrix or the model design sheet or the workmanship standard, re-verify affected units

iteration_protocol.trigger: the week-one review finds flooded, silent or misrouted alerts, or unread reports
iteration_protocol.action: retune thresholds, recipients and the report set against observed behavior; prune unconsumed config

iteration_protocol.trigger: driver pushback, a grievance, or an unplug cluster after rollout
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the disclosure conversation with the policy on the table, check monitoring scope against what was disclosed, and flag any jurisdictional question for verification

iteration_protocol.trigger: buffered, missing or teleporting tracks cluster in an area marked covered
iteration_protocol.action: re-walk the coverage qualification for that area, correct the notes, and brief the admin on the artifact before it becomes a confidence crisis

iteration_protocol.trigger: the fleet changes - vehicles added or sold, a new yard, crews reorganized, take-home policy introduced
iteration_protocol.action: re-open intake for the delta, update matrix, account structure, fences and disclosure as affected, and run the per-unit pipeline for new units

iteration_protocol.trigger: an acceptance exception passes its fix date or operations disputes an early fault's origin
iteration_protocol.action: escalate the exception with its verification and triage records, resolve ownership, and close or re-date the item with the customer

19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
